sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface display confirmed by PI-PLC shedding assay (human HA-GPC4, L1/L2); function NOT MEASURED for the human HA-tagged construct. Zebrafish GFP-Gpc4 ortholog rescued C&E defects in gpc4 mutants (L5), confirming functional integrity of the post-SP insertion in the ortholog.
sites.rationale: GPC4 is a GPI-anchored protein whose signal peptide spans residues 1–18 (authoritative landmarks). An N-terminal HA tag on a full-length, membrane-anchored construct must reside after the SP cleavage site (residue 18) to survive to the cell surface; a tag upstream would be co-translationally cleaved with the SP. Python confirms residue 18 = A and residue 19 = A. The zebrafish ortholog evidence (L3–L6) independently places GFP at the equivalent post-SP junction and demonstrates functional rescue, strongly corroborating this as the tolerated insertion point. No other extracellular junction is named anywhere in the ledger. PMC8387153 (L1/L2): full-length human GPC4 with an N-terminal HA tag (pCAG nHA GPC4) expressed in HEK293T cells; PI-PLC treatment released the tagged protein into conditioned media, confirming GPI-anchored surface display of the HA-tagged construct. No specific residue number is stated for the tag junction. Corroborated by PMC8488972 (L3–L6): zebrafish Gpc4 ortholog with EGFP inserted immediately after its signal peptide (AA1–23), expressed on the plasma membrane of endodermal cells and functionally rescuing convergence-and-extension defects in gpc4 mutants.

sources.claim: N-terminal HA-tagged GPC4 was transfected into HEK293T cells, and media were collected with and without PI-PLC treatment ( Fig. 1 B ).

literature_notes: All six ledger lines converge on a single site: the N-terminal extracellular junction immediately after the signal peptide cleavage site (after residue 18). L1 and L2 are direct human GPC4 evidence (HA tag, surface confirmed by PI-PLC); L3–L6 are zebrafish Gpc4 ortholog evidence (GFP after SP AA1–23, surface-localised and functionally validated). Because both papers describe the same conceptual junction—post-signal-peptide on the extracellular N-terminus—this is one site, not two. No ledger line names any internal loop insertion, any C-terminal tag, or any intracellular position for GPC4/Gpc4. The C-terminal GPI anchor signal (roughly residues ~491–556) is cleaved during GPI attachment, making a C-terminal surface tag structurally impossible; no ledger line proposes one. No abrogating insertions are reported in the ledger.
